note: What a shell owes each guest publication that answers no host call (ticket 26/09/30/NON-DESTRUCTIVE-HISTORY-EDITING, live fault F11). A typed operation outlives the command that started it: its completion (`completed: true`, `AppFrame::OperationCompleted`) is the only carrier of its dirty scope and its command-log delta, and a long run pushes UI-progress frames (`completed: false`) meanwhile. `publication` is one entry exactly as a host queues it and hands it on; `queued` says whether it is worth queueing at all (a completion that dirtied nothing and patched nothing is bookkeeping — a retained operation completes on every drain poll); `refresh` is the dirty scope the shell owes it, with NO further dispatch; `told` says whether the person is told a notice. A history patch is always folded, whatever the refresh. A completion that patched history and dirtied nothing else owes the reserved History body (`historyBodyKey`) the row it minted; progress with a patch alone moves the band and re-renders nothing; `fault` is the host drain's own failure and is never silence; `resync` says a bounded queue (`capacity` entries) gave up entries, so the shell re-reads the whole history projection and refreshes everything.
